question: linux-x1 measured zero instruction movement across the comment cleanup on ARM GNU 14.2.1 and said it could not speak for the other benches' compilers. This is the same gate on ARM GNU 14.3.1, the project's other code generator.
instrument: tools/image_mnemonics.py at 766c951 - the FIXED tool - run against both ELFs of every pair. The copy at 75b6f60 absorbs trailing data into the preceding symbol, so using each revision's own tool would compare a buggy hash against a fixed one.
method: One worktree (C:/Jerry.Projects/dso-old), two checkouts, fixed build-directory names, so build-path length is constant across each pair. This is the confound linux-x1 retracted: absolute __FILE__ strings inside the image made the reported count track the length of the build directory.

positive_control.what: one __asm__ volatile("nop") inserted as the first statement of main() in apps/baremetal_bringup/main.c, Track B, built at the same path and hashed with the same tool, then reverted
positive_control.why: a hash that cannot detect a change produces the same all-identical table for the wrong reason, so the gate was broken on purpose on THIS bench rather than trusted from linux-x1's
positive_control.means: the hash discriminates - it moved. The INSTRUCTION COUNT DID NOT, because the injected nop consumed existing alignment padding.
positive_control.the_catch: An independent instance of mac-bench's #54 caution, where 10 of 18 differing functions had identical counts. A count is a far weaker instrument than a hash: anything reasoning from text size or n_instructions alone can miss a real code change. Quote the hash, not the count.

behaviour.board: attached, control channel not console fallback

settling_run.note: after a forced --reflash; reported but NOT relied on - this bench does not believe the first suite after a flash

behaviour.vs_linux_x1: their 585/16/2 differs by one test in a column, not in a total: test_host_fed_ramp_loses_no_samples[b] is a runtime-conditional xfail on #24's signature that alternates run to run, documented in docs/testing.md section 7. It landed on the pass side in both runs here.

reflash_is_not_optional: The suite flashes only when the board's TRACK disagrees with --track. A new image of a track the board already runs is silently not flashed, and the run then measures the old firmware while reporting a clean pass.
not_claimed: that these hashes should match linux-x1's - they are a different code generator and 10,342 against their 10,510 on Track B is expected
that Track A still BEHAVES correctly here - only its image was gated; its suite was not run
that tools/dso_metrics.py is exercised - test_scope.py skips 4 cases on this bench for want of a bench scope, the same gap linux-x1 reported
that the settling run is evidence of anything beyond agreeing with the measured one
